### Step 1 — Scene
A breakfast plate of shredded hash browns topped with salsa, bacon strips, and what appears to be a dark, well-browned sausage link.

### Step 2 — Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### Steps 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area shares below partition the visible food coverage; salsa-covered areas are not counted again as exposed potatoes.

| Item | Plate area | Area × typical height = volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fried shredded hash browns | 42% | 223 cm² × 1.4 cm = 312 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 203 g | 200 | 406 kcal |
| Green salsa with diced tomato/onion | 10% | 53 cm² × 0.6 cm = 32 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 32 g | 30 | 10 kcal |
| Cooked bacon strips | 14% | 74 cm² × 0.4 cm = 30 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 27 g | 540 | 146 kcal |
| Browned breakfast sausage, tentative identification | 6% | 32 cm² × 1.5 cm = 48 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 46 g | 320 | 147 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 42% + 10% + 14% + 6% = **72%** of the plate. Cooking fat is included in the hash browns’ energy density; no separately measurable oil pool is visible.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **308 g and about 710 kcal**, plausible for a moderately piled potato breakfast with calorie-dense bacon and sausage. The dark item’s identity and the potatoes’ oil content are the main uncertainties.
